_format: The bundled sound sequence catalogue. Each entry is copied into config/hex/sounds.json when the player
adds it, so `sequence` is exactly the shape that file uses and can be pasted straight into it.
presetId  stable identity, never reused for a different preset. Names two lang keys:
hex.sound.preset.<presetId>.name and .desc. It is also the id an installed copy is given, so
a freshly added Alarm is referenced as "@alarm" everywhere a sound can be chosen.
revision  bump whenever the definition below changes. An installed copy the player has NOT edited is
updated in place on the next launch; an edited one is left alone and offered the update. The
id is never changed by an update, so every "@id" pointing at it keeps working.
category  grouping in the browser. Names hex.sounds.presets.category.<category>
sequence.bpm        the editor's grid only. Playback reads atMillis, which is already absolute, so
changing this re-rules the grid without moving a single step.
sequence.loop       whether the whole thing repeats; loopCount is how many passes in total (1-8).
sequence.steps[]    sound    a sound event id. Never a "@ref" - a step may not name another sequence.
atMillis when it plays, in milliseconds from the start. Absolute, not a delay.
pitch    0.5-2.0. For a note_block sound this is a note: pitch = 2^((n-12)/12),
so 0.5 is F#3, 1.0 is F#4 and 2.0 is F#5. The editor shows the note name.
volume   0.0-1.0. Drawn as the clip's fill height in the editor.
lane     0-7. Presentational only - two steps at the same time play together
whatever lanes they are on.
Keep these short. They are alert sounds, and one that outlasts the thing it is announcing is a nuisance.
